messages:
sasha (platform): morning — quick UX/API question about the rollout dashboard: do we show configured pct or effective routed weight after quota caps? thinking about per-customer quota + dedicated pools making UI % != real traffic. :thinking:

david (eng-platform): we currently surface the configured split only. that’s what release owners expect to set, but it breaks the canary vs baseline metrics when quotas kick in.

jing (eng-runtime): observed weight is the truth for metrics. if UI says 20% canary but runtime routed 5% because of quota fallback, alerts and deltas are misleading.

emma (devex): for A/B tests we should surface both: configured (what you intended) + observed (what actually hit the variant). label them clearly and show a small sparkline for the last 1h.

sasha (platform): idea: two side-by-side numbers — "configured split" and "effective split (1h)" with reason tags (e.g., quota, model-fallback, region-constraint). also a lightweight tooltip explaining discrepancy.

david (eng-platform): mid-debate: API shape. current rollout proto has `traffic_percent` as an int. proposal: add `effective_weight` (float) + `weight_source` enum + `quota_reasons` array. do we keep both percent and fraction?

jing (eng-runtime): prefer explicit fields: `configured_weight` (float), `effective_weight` (float), `weight_source` ("configured"|"runtime"|"quota_adjusted"). avoid duplicating percent vs fraction; use floats with a sane formatter in UI.

sasha (platform): ok. also need to agree what alerts should use: observed or configured? my take: SLA/health alerts -> observed. rollout-gate (block release) -> configured vs baseline quality metrics.

david (eng-platform): agreed. implement alerts to evaluate against observed deltas. add optional guard that compares against configured expected and raises a warning (not a fail) if configured != observed.

deploy-bot: Deploy triggered for canary/1748001234 by @sasha; sha f3a1b9d — rolling updates to 3 nodes.

jing (eng-runtime): extra runtime note: need minimum traffic threshold before we compute stable deltas. small slices are noisy — show median + 95% CI. if requests < threshold, show "insufficient data" instead of a spurious delta.

emma (devex): UX suggestion: a per-route toggle for "show observed vs configured" and a per-rollout control for min traffic (default 100 req / 5m). show a grey badge when below threshold.

sasha (platform): proposing API change and a tiny dashboard tweak: add `effective_weight`, `weight_source`, `quota_reasons[]` to rollout status. I'll open a PR with schema + dashboard wireframes.

david (eng-platform): sgtm. can you paste a short example rollout object so runtime folks know exact keys?

sasha (platform): sure — example:```
{
  "rollout_id": "canary-42",
  "configured_weight": 0.20,
  "effective_weight": 0.0523,
  "weight_source": "quota_adjusted",
  "quota_reasons": ["customer_cap:acct_1234","region_pool_exhausted"],
  "observed_window": "60m",
  "observed_requests": 512
}
```

jing (eng-runtime): that shape works. will add the runtime field mappings and a fallback metric we can emit: `rollout.effective_weight` as a gauge. also will include `rollout.quota_reasons` as tags in logs.

sasha (platform): nice. david — can you add an alert rule template to the PR? something like "trigger if observed_delta(metric) > 10% for 5m AND observed_requests >= 100".

david (eng-platform): yup will sketch it out.

emma (devex): I'll update wireframes to include the CI bars and the insufficient-data badge.

sasha (platform): thanks all. i'll open the PR and tag @david @jing for review. moving to implement next sprint. :rocket:
